sections.h2: Where are Hays County property records kept?
sections.html:
The Hays County Clerk's Records Division keeps the county's official public records, which run from 1848 to the present and include deeds, deeds of trust and liens. You can view and buy copies through the clerk's online Self-Service portal or on the computers in the office lobby, and archived record books can be read in the office. For questions about official public records, the Records Division lists the address recordsdivision@hayscountytx.gov.

The clerk's office has three divisions: Records, Courts and Commissioners Court. Probate and guardianship support sits with the Courts Division, which matters when the owner of a house has died. Divorce and family court files are held by the District Clerk, so a title question that involves a divorce decree may need a stop at that office too.

San Marcos is the main site, and the clerk also runs three substations. Each is listed Monday through Friday, 8 am to 4:30 pm, closed from noon to 1 pm:

  • Precinct 2, Kyle: 5458 FM 2770, Suite 120, phone 512-878-6687
  • Precinct 3, Wimberley: 200 Stillwater, Suite 101, phone 512-878-6684
  • Precinct 4, Dripping Springs: 195 Roger Hanks Pkwy, Suite 113, phone 512-878-6683

Call before you drive to a substation and confirm it takes the filing you have in hand.

sections.h2: How do I search Hays County land records online?
sections.html:
Use the clerk's Self-Service portal, which opens on a disclaimer you must accept before searching. The disclaimer says the clerk does not certify the information shown, that the index works like a library card catalogue, and that you should try every spelling variation of a name. Treat the index as a pointer to the recorded document, and read the document itself before you rely on it.

When you check a Hays County house before a sale, these searches catch most surprises:

  • Every owner name on the chain of title, with and without middle initials, suffixes and former surnames.
  • Each deed of trust, then a matching release. A loan paid off years ago can still show as open if the release was never filed.
  • Judgments, abstracts and state tax liens. The state clerk manual says the Comptroller files state tax lien notices with the county clerk, who records them in a state tax lien book.
  • Notices of foreclosure sale, which the clerk posts and files.

The clerk also offers Fraud Guard, a free service that emails you when a document carrying your name is recorded. It is a cheap early warning against a forged deed on a rental house or vacant lot.

sections.h2: What makes a deed recordable in Hays County?
sections.html:
A deed can be recorded only if it is signed and acknowledged before a notary or another authorized officer, or sworn before two subscribing witnesses (Property Code 12.001(b)). The deed goes to the county clerk of the county where the land sits so a house in Kyle, Wimberley or Dripping Springs is recorded with the Hays County Clerk.

The state clerk manual lists the usual instruments in the deed records: general and special warranty deeds, quitclaim deeds, trustee's deeds, sheriff's deeds, tax deeds, affidavits, releases of deeds of trust, leases, contracts of sale and powers of attorney. It also sets the fee building blocks. The first page is $5.00 and each added page is $4.00, with several smaller county fees for records management, archives and technology on top. A missing grantee mailing address can add $25. Ask the Hays clerk for the current total before you send a check.

The same manual notes that commissioners courts may direct clerks to waive real property recording fees for buyers who use certain federal or state grant programs. If a buyer in your sale is using one, ask whether Hays County has adopted that waiver.

sections.h2: Who sets value and bills tax in Hays County?
sections.html:
Two offices handle the money side, and neither is the clerk. The Hays Central Appraisal District in Kyle sets value, runs the property search, and processes exemptions, while the Hays County Tax Office sends bills and takes payments. The district says plainly that it does not send tax bills or process payments of any kind.

The district lists 21001 North IH 35, Kyle, phone (512) 268-2522, open Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with a drop box at the front door. Its online forms cover a homestead exemption, an agricultural use application, a business personal property rendition and a change of address. Bills and payment instructions are on the county tax office site at tax.co.hays.tx.us.

Hays CAD also audits every granted homestead once every five years under Tax Code 11.43(h-1). An owner who gets an audit letter should answer it with a copy of a valid Texas driver's license or state ID whose address matches the house. If the letter is ignored, the exemption gets a termination date. Statewide, values are set as of January 1, notices for homesteads go out around April 1, and a protest generally must be filed by May 15 or 30 days after the notice is delivered, whichever is later.

sections.h2: Which record problems slow a Hays County house sale?
sections.html:
The usual culprits are old liens, unpaid tax and missing heirs. Texas puts a tax lien on property every January 1 to secure that year's tax, so an unpaid bill follows the house even after a sale. A bill left unpaid after January 31 becomes delinquent on February 1, when a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest are added.

Inherited houses add their own steps:

  • A transfer on death deed must be recorded before the owner dies, in the county where the property sits.
  • A muniment of title order and the will are filed with the county clerk of the county where the property is.
  • An affidavit of heirship is a sworn statement filed with the clerk, and no law forces a buyer or title company to accept it.
  • Heirs who are not named on a recorded deed need to give the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership interest, a death certificate and a recent utility bill to get the homestead exemption.

Foreclosure notices are also filed with the county clerk, at least 21 days before the first-Tuesday auction. If a notice is on file against a Hays County house, the title company will treat the sale as urgent.

faqs.q: Which office records a deed in Hays County?
faqs.a: The Hays County Clerk's Records Division records deeds, deeds of trust and liens, and its records go back to 1848. File with the clerk of the county where the property sits, which for a Hays County house is the Hays County Clerk.

faqs.q: Can I search Hays County deeds online?
faqs.a: Yes, through the clerk's Self-Service portal, where records can be viewed and purchased. The portal asks you to accept a disclaimer first, and it advises trying every spelling of a name.

faqs.q: Does the appraisal district record my deed?
faqs.a: No. Hays Central Appraisal District sets value and handles exemptions from its Kyle office, while the clerk records the deed. Owners usually update the district separately, for example by using its online change of address form.

faqs.q: Who sends the Hays County property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Hays County Tax Office sends bills and takes payments. The appraisal district says it does not send bills or process any payment, so call the tax office about a bill.

faqs.q: What happens if a deed has no grantee mailing address?
faqs.a: The clerk may add a $25 charge. Put a mailing address for every buyer on the deed before you file.
